title: Beyond SOFA and APACHE II, Novel Risk Stratification Models Using Readily Available Biomarkers in Critical Care.
summary: A 19,720-patient ICU cohort produced a logistic risk model using biomarker ratios, ventilation and CRRT that internally discriminated in-hospital mortality (AUC 0.929), comparable to SOFA (0.931); the paper does not establish superiority or external generalization. The study does not establish external generalization, causal effects or sustained operational impact.
ai_technology: XGBoost/SHAP ranks predictors before logistic mortality models; the enabled outcome is ICU mortality risk stratification.
organization: Department of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery, Samsung Medical Center, Sungkyunkwan University School of Medicine, Seoul 06351, Republic of Korea

evidence.tested: The primary Results report 666 deaths and Model 3 (LAR, NPAR, mechanical ventilation, CRRT) AUC 0.929 (95% CI 0.921–0.937); SOFA AUC 0.931 and DeLong p=0.052. This supports a bounded internally tested clinical prediction result, not claimed improvement over SOFA.
evidence.unknown: Primary Methods describe repeated 70/30 train/test splits; Results also report 10-fold internal cross-validation. No external cohort is reported, and the split descriptions are not fully consistent; conclusions are limited to internal retrospective performance.
evidence.ai_role: XGBoost/SHAP ranks predictors before logistic mortality models; the enabled outcome is ICU mortality risk stratification.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
